components.note: 日 (sun) — the sun beside the moon: two light sources, so bright and clear.
月 (moon) — as in 朋, 期, 有; here it brightens the night.
年 (year) — first drawn as a person carrying harvested grain: one harvest per year. Seen in 今年, 去年, 年轻.

example.hanzi: 我们明年会搬到新家。
example.pinyin: wǒmen míngnián huì bān dào xīn jiā.
example.english: We will move to a new home next year.
example.fact: Earth actually takes about 365.24 days to orbit the sun, so the calendar adds a leap day nearly every four years to stay in sync. The Gregorian calendar refines this further by skipping the leap day in century years not divisible by 400, which is why 1900 wasn't a leap year but 2000 was. Without these corrections, our calendar would drift by roughly a full day every century.

examples.hanzi: 你明年打算做什么？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ míngnián dǎsuàn zuò shénme?
examples.english: What do you plan to do next year?

examples.hanzi: 我弟弟明年就要上大学了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ dìdi míngnián jiù yào shàng dàxué le.
examples.english: My younger brother is going to university next year.

components.note: 忄 (heart) — marks the mind and feelings, as in 情, 快, 忙; 懂 is to understand.
董 (dǒng) gives the sound exactly: 懂 dǒng.
彳 (step) — walking and going, as in 行, 往, 很 very.
寸 (hand) — oldest form is a hand grabbing a cowrie shell (money): 得 is "to obtain". The shell has worn down to 旦.

example.hanzi: 她懂得如何安慰别人。
example.pinyin: tā dǒngde rúhé ānwèi biérén.
example.english: She knows how to comfort others.
example.fact: For over a thousand years, no one could read ancient Egyptian hieroglyphs until the Rosetta Stone was discovered by French soldiers in 1799. The stone carried the same decree in three scripts, including Greek, which scholars already understood. French linguist Jean-François Champollion used it to crack the code in 1822, finally letting historians understand millennia of Egyptian writing.

examples.hanzi: 他不懂得照顾自己。
examples.pinyin: Tā bù dǒngde zhàogù zìjǐ.
examples.english: He doesn't know how to take care of himself.

examples.hanzi: 我们要懂得感谢帮助过我们的人。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yào dǒngde gǎnxiè bāngzhù guo wǒmen de rén.
examples.english: We should know to be grateful to those who have helped us.

components.note: 扌 (hand radical, 提手旁) — arranging and moving by hand: 打, 推, 拉; 排 is to line things up.
非 (fēi) is a loose sound hint; its series includes 悲 bēi and 菲 fēi.
阝 on the left is 阜 (steps, hill) — as in 院, 阳, 阴: 除 first meant palace steps; to step away, remove.
余 (yú) is a loose sound clue for chú; 余 also in 涂 tú, 途 tú and 徐 xú.

example.hanzi: 医生排除了其他疾病的可能。
example.pinyin: yīshēng páichú le qítā jíbìng de kěnéng.
example.english: The doctor ruled out other possible illnesses.
example.fact: Smallpox is the only human infectious disease ever to be completely eradicated worldwide, a milestone declared by the World Health Organization in 1980. It took a coordinated global vaccination campaign lasting over a decade to rule out the disease region by region. The last natural case occurred in Somalia in 1977, ending a disease that had killed an estimated 300 million people in the 20th century alone.

examples.hanzi: 医生已经排除了这种可能。
examples.pinyin: Yīshēng yǐjīng páichú le zhè zhǒng kěnéng.
examples.english: The doctor has already ruled out this possibility.

examples.hanzi: 我们要排除一切困难。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yào páichú yíqiè kùnnan.
examples.english: We have to eliminate all difficulties.

components.note: 小 (small) — three small dots, tiny grains. As a radical it appears in 少 few, 尖 sharp.
子 (child) — children and offspring, as in 孙 grandchild, 学 study, 字 character; 孩 is a young child.
亥 (hài) is a close sound clue for hái; 亥 also sounds out 该 gāi, 核 hé and 刻 kè.
子 (child) — a picture of a baby with arms outstretched and legs bundled. As a suffix (孩子, 房子) it is a light noun ending.

example.hanzi: 那个小孩子在公园里玩耍。
example.pinyin: nàge xiǎoháizi zài gōngyuán lǐ wánshuǎ.
example.english: That child is playing in the park.
example.fact: A human child's brain reaches about 90 percent of its adult size by age five, even though the rest of the body has years of growing left to do. This rapid early brain development is why the first few years of life are considered critical for language and cognitive skills. Researchers estimate the brain forms over a million new neural connections every second during this period.

examples.hanzi: 几个小孩子在门口玩游戏。
examples.pinyin: Jǐ ge xiǎoháizi zài ménkǒu wán yóuxì.
examples.english: A few small children are playing a game at the door.

examples.hanzi: 小孩子不要喝咖啡。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎoháizi búyào hē kāfēi.
examples.english: Little kids shouldn't drink coffee.

meanings: sweet (commonly used to describe a girl or woman)

components.note: 氵 (water) — marks water, as in 河, 海, 汤; 温 is warm, like lukewarm water.
昷 (wēn) gives the sound exactly: 温 wēn, also in 瘟 wēn.
木 (wood) — marks wood and plants, as in 林, 树, 桥; 柔 is pliable wood.
矛 (máo) is a loose hint for róu; 揉 róu shares the same part.

example.hanzi: 她说话总是很温柔。
example.pinyin: tā shuōhuà zǒngshì hěn wēnróu.
example.english: She always speaks very gently.
example.fact: Whale sharks are the largest fish in the ocean, growing up to 18 meters long, yet they are gentle filter feeders that pose no threat to humans. They swim slowly near the surface with their mouths open, straining plankton and small fish from the water. Divers around the world seek them out specifically because they tolerate close human contact so calmly.

examples.hanzi: 妈妈温柔地抱着孩子。
examples.pinyin: Māma wēnróu de bào zhe háizi.
examples.english: Mom is holding the baby gently.

examples.hanzi: 她的声音又轻又温柔。
examples.pinyin: Tā de shēngyīn yòu qīng yòu wēnróu.
examples.english: Her voice is soft and gentle.

components.note: 欠 (open mouth, yawn) — marks mouths, wanting and owing, as in 歌 song, 欢 joy, 款 funds; 欲 is craving.
谷 (yù) gives the sound exactly: 欲 yù, also in 浴 yù and 裕 yù.

example.hanzi: 孩子的求知欲很强。
example.pinyin: Háizi de qiúzhīyù hěn qiáng.
example.english: The child has a strong desire for knowledge.
example.fact: 欲 names a 'desire' noun and attaches to words such as 食欲 (appetite), 求知欲 (thirst for knowledge) and 购买欲 (urge to buy). As a verb, 欲 + verb is a formal 'about to', as in 欲言又止 'wanting to speak but holding back'.

examples.hanzi: 我今天没有食欲。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ jīntiān méiyǒu shíyù.
examples.english: I have no appetite today.

examples.hanzi: 她想去旅行的欲望很强。
examples.pinyin: Tā xiǎng qù lǚxíng de yùwàng hěn qiáng.
examples.english: Her desire to travel is strong.

components.note: 大 (person) — a man with a hairpin 一 on his head, a grown man; 夫 also gives 扶 fú and 肤 fū.
女 (woman) — women and family, as in 妈, 她, 姐; oldest form shows a hand arranging a woman's hair, a wife.

example.hanzi: 他们是一对幸福的夫妻。
example.pinyin: tāmen shì yī duì xìngfú de fūqī.
example.english: They are a happy married couple.
example.fact: Wandering albatrosses often mate for life and can remain paired with the same partner for decades, reuniting each breeding season after months apart at sea. Because raising a single chick takes so long, pairs that stay together year after year raise their young more successfully than birds that switch partners. Some tracked pairs have been recorded together for more than 50 years.

examples.hanzi: 这对夫妻都在医院工作。
examples.pinyin: Zhè duì fūqī dōu zài yīyuàn gōngzuò.
examples.english: This married couple both work at the hospital.

examples.hanzi: 夫妻之间要多沟通。
examples.pinyin: Fūqī zhījiān yào duō gōutōng.
examples.english: Husbands and wives should communicate more.

components.note: 成 (chéng) is a sound clue for 城 chéng, 诚 chéng and 盛 chéng: the same sound.
交 (cross, hand over) — a person with legs crossed: to intersect, then to exchange. Same part in 校 xiào, 较 jiào, 胶 jiāo.

example.hanzi: 这笔生意终于成交了。
example.pinyin: zhè bǐ shēngyì zhōngyú chéngjiāo le.
example.english: This business deal was finally closed.
example.fact: In 1867, the United States bought Alaska from the Russian Empire for $7.2 million, or about two cents an acre. At the time critics mocked the deal as 'Seward's Folly' after Secretary of State William Seward, who negotiated it. The purchase turned out to hold vast oil and mineral reserves worth far more than its original price.

examples.hanzi: 这套房子以三百万成交。
examples.pinyin: Zhè tào fángzi yǐ sānbǎi wàn chéngjiāo.
examples.english: This house was sold for three million.

examples.hanzi: 如果你同意这个价格，我们现在就成交。
examples.pinyin: Rúguǒ nǐ tóngyì zhège jiàgé, wǒmen xiànzài jiù chéngjiāo.
examples.english: If you agree to this price, we'll close the deal now.

components.note: 王 (king) — the ruler below the crown-like top: 皇 is an emperor, as in 皇帝.
皇 (huáng) as a part sounds out 凰 huáng, 煌 huáng and 惶 huáng.
后 (after, behind) — two words merged in simplified writing: old 后 "ruler" (皇后 empress) and 後 "behind, later" (as in 然后).

example.hanzi: 皇后住在宫殿的最深处。
example.pinyin: huánghòu zhù zài gōngdiàn de zuì shēn chù.
example.english: The empress lives in the deepest part of the palace.
example.fact: Wu Zetian ruled China from 690 to 705 AD as its only officially recognized female emperor, having risen from a former royal concubine to head of state. She restructured the civil examination system to recruit officials based on merit rather than birth alone, expanding opportunities beyond the aristocracy. Her reign is still debated by historians, some crediting her with genuine reform and others painting her as ruthlessly opportunistic.

examples.hanzi: 国王和皇后坐在大厅里。
examples.pinyin: Guówáng hé huánghòu zuò zài dàtīng lǐ.
examples.english: The king and queen are sitting in the hall.

examples.hanzi: 这位皇后很受人民喜爱。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi huánghòu hěn shòu rénmín xǐ'ài.
examples.english: This queen is much loved by the people.

components.note: 壴 (drum) — a picture of a drum on a stand; 鼓 adds a hand with a stick 支 beating it.
力 (strength) — marks effort, as in 动 move, 努 strive, 办; 励 is to urge on.
厉 (lì) gives the sound exactly: 励 lì.

example.hanzi: 老师鼓励学生多提问题。
example.pinyin: lǎoshī gǔlì xuésheng duō tí wèntí.
example.english: The teacher encourages students to ask more questions.
example.fact: Psychologist B.F. Skinner's mid-20th-century experiments with rats and pigeons showed that behavior followed by a reward is repeated far more often than behavior that isn't. He called this principle operant conditioning, and it became a foundation of modern behavioral psychology and education. The same principle explains why simple, well-timed encouragement can be more effective at shaping habits than punishment.

examples.hanzi: 父母的鼓励让我更有信心。
examples.pinyin: Fùmǔ de gǔlì ràng wǒ gèng yǒu xìnxīn.
examples.english: My parents' encouragement gave me more confidence.

examples.hanzi: 朋友们都鼓励他去试一试。
examples.pinyin: Péngyoumen dōu gǔlì tā qù shì yi shì.
examples.english: His friends all encouraged him to give it a try.

components.note: ⺮ (bamboo) — ⺮ is bamboo, as in 笔, 筷, 箱; slips of bamboo were written on, so 签 is a slip or to sign.
佥 (qiān) — same sound — 签 is qiān; 佥 also sounds out 检 jiǎn and 脸 liǎn.
宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家, 安, 室.
子 (child) — a child in a house: to bear and nurture; characters were later "born" from other characters.

example.hanzi: 请在这份合同上签字。
example.pinyin: qǐng zài zhè fèn hétong shàng qiānzì.
example.english: Please sign this contract.
example.fact: The Magna Carta was sealed by King John of England at Runnymede in 1215 after English barons rebelled against his abuses of power. It was one of the first documents to state that even a king was bound by the law, a radical idea at the time. Though most of its specific clauses are no longer in force, its core principle influenced constitutional law across the world, including the U.S. Constitution.

examples.hanzi: 签字之前请先仔细看一遍。
examples.pinyin: Qiānzì zhīqián qǐng xiān zǐxì kàn yí biàn.
examples.english: Please read it carefully before signing.

examples.hanzi: 他看完文件就签字了。
examples.pinyin: Tā kàn wán wénjiàn jiù qiānzì le.
examples.english: He signed after reading the document.

components.note: 耳 (ear) — a picture of an ear; as a radical it marks hearing, as in 闻, 聪, 聊.

example.hanzi: 他在我耳边小声说话。
example.pinyin: Tā zài wǒ ěr biān xiǎoshēng shuōhuà.
example.english: He spoke quietly by my ear.
example.fact: In daily speech the ear is 耳朵; the single character 耳 is used in compounds like 耳机 (earphones) and 耳环 (earring). In classical writing 耳 also marks 'and that's all', like 而已.

examples.hanzi: 请戴上耳机。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng dàishàng ěrjī.
examples.english: Please put on the earphones.

examples.hanzi: 他的耳朵有点疼。
examples.pinyin: Tā de ěrduo yǒudiǎn téng.
examples.english: His ear hurts a little.

components.note: 今 (jīn) — the top part hints the sound — 金 is jīn, like 今; 金 means gold and metal.
金 (metal) — as a radical it shrinks to 钅 in simplified characters — 钱 money, 铁 iron, 钟 clock, 银 silver.
钅 (metal) — 钅 is the simplified 金 (metal), as in 铁, 银, 钟; early money was metal coins.
戋 (jiān) — near sound — 钱 is qián; 戋 also sounds out 浅 qiǎn and 线 xiàn, and means small or thin.

example.hanzi: 金钱买不到真正的快乐。
example.pinyin: jīnqián mǎibudào zhēnzhèng de kuàilè.
example.english: Money can't buy true happiness.
example.fact: The Lydians, in what is now western Turkey, are credited with minting the first standardized metal coins around 600 BC, made from a natural gold-silver alloy called electrum. Before that, most trade relied on bartering goods or weighing out precious metal by hand. Standardized coinage made trade faster and more reliable because merchants no longer had to verify the weight and purity of metal for every transaction.

examples.hanzi: 他把金钱看得太重了。
examples.pinyin: Tā bǎ jīnqián kàn de tài zhòng le.
examples.english: He puts too much importance on money.

examples.hanzi: 这些金钱我们要用在孩子的教育上。
examples.pinyin: Zhèxiē jīnqián wǒmen yào yòng zài háizi de jiàoyù shàng.
examples.english: We will spend this money on our children's education.

meanings: to the best of one's ability

components.note: 尺 (chǐ, ruler) — the visible top part, as in 尺寸 size. 尽 simplifies 盡 and the shape does not explain 'use up'. Memory aid: measure it to the very end.
口 (mouth) — speech or assent: to say "OK". 可 is also a famous sound part: 河 hé, 歌 gē, 哥 gē, 何 hé all take their sound from it.
能 (can) — originally a picture of a bear, a strong animal (熊 xióng adds fire 灬); "strong, able" gave "can".

example.hanzi: 我们要尽可能节省时间。
example.pinyin: wǒmen yào jǐnkěnéng jiéshěng shíjiān.
example.english: We should save time as much as possible.
example.fact: When Edmund Hillary and Tenzing Norgay reached the summit of Mount Everest in 1953, they were pushing the absolute limit of what human physiology could endure at 8,849 meters, where the air holds roughly a third of the oxygen found at sea level. Climbers today still train for years and use supplemental oxygen to survive as high as possible above the 'death zone' near the peak. Even with modern gear, dozens of people still die on the mountain's slopes most years.

examples.hanzi: 请尽可能早点到。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng jǐnkěnéng zǎodiǎn dào.
examples.english: Please arrive as early as possible.

examples.hanzi: 他尽可能地帮助每一个人。
examples.pinyin: Tā jǐnkěnéng de bāngzhù měi yí ge rén.
examples.english: He helps everyone as much as he can.

components.note: 讠 (speech, from 言) — marks talk and language, as in 说, 语, 话; 读 is to read aloud.
卖 (mài) is only a loose hint for dú; it stands in for an older 賣, as in 牍 dú and 犊 dú.
书 (simplified 書) — the old form shows a brush 聿 writing; to write, then what is written: book, letter.

example.hanzi: 他每天晚上都读书。
example.pinyin: tā měitiān wǎnshàng dōu dúshū.
example.english: He reads every night.
example.fact: The Library of Alexandria, founded in Egypt around the 3rd century BC, is estimated to have held several hundred thousand scrolls, making it one of the largest collections of knowledge in the ancient world. Scholars there made major advances in mathematics, astronomy, and medicine, aided by access to texts gathered from across the Mediterranean and beyond. Much of its collection was lost over centuries of political turmoil, and historians still debate exactly how and when it was ultimately destroyed.

examples.hanzi: 他在大学读书，学的是历史。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài dàxué dúshū, xué de shì lìshǐ.
examples.english: He's studying at university, majoring in history.

examples.hanzi: 我喜欢在咖啡馆里读书。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xǐhuan zài kāfēiguǎn lǐ dúshū.
examples.english: I like reading in cafes.

components.note: 成 (chéng) is a sound clue for 城 chéng, 诚 chéng and 盛 chéng: the same sound.
京 (jīng, high mound, capital) is a loose sound clue for jiù; going up to a high place fits 就 "to approach, to go to".

example.hanzi: 这是他一生最大的成就。
example.pinyin: zhè shì tā yīshēng zuìdà de chéngjiù.
example.english: This is the greatest achievement of his life.
example.fact: On July 20, 1969, Apollo 11 astronauts Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin became the first humans to walk on the moon, fulfilling a goal President Kennedy had set less than a decade earlier. The entire guidance computer that got them there had less processing power than a modern digital watch. Around 600 million people, roughly a sixth of the world's population at the time, watched the landing live on television.

examples.hanzi: 他的成就让大家都很骄傲。
examples.pinyin: Tā de chéngjiù ràng dàjiā dōu hěn jiāo'ào.
examples.english: His achievements make everyone very proud.

examples.hanzi: 这家公司取得了很大的成就。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā gōngsī qǔdé le hěn dà de chéngjiù.
examples.english: This company has made great achievements.

components.note: 攵 (tap, hand with stick) — actions applied to people: 放, 改, 政; 教 is to teach, traditionally with a rod.
孝 (xiào) is a near sound match for jiào; also in 酵 jiào.
会 (meet, can) — simplified from 會, a lid on a container: bringing things together; hence meeting, then "can" (huì).

example.hanzi: 老师教会了我们很多知识。
example.pinyin: lǎoshī jiāohuì le wǒmen hěn duō zhīshi.
example.english: The teacher taught us a lot of knowledge.
example.fact: Finland's education system is often ranked among the world's best, and one reason is that teachers there must complete a master's degree before entering the classroom. Finnish schools also assign relatively little homework and delay formal reading instruction until around age seven, trusting play-based early learning instead. Despite this seemingly relaxed approach, Finnish students consistently score near the top of international assessments.

examples.hanzi: 这座教会在这个城市已经一百年了。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zuò jiàohuì zài zhège chéngshì yǐjīng yì bǎi nián le.
examples.english: This church has been in the city for a hundred years.

examples.hanzi: 她每个星期天都去教会。
examples.pinyin: Tā měi ge xīngqītiān dōu qù jiàohuì.
examples.english: She goes to church every Sunday.

components.note: 耂 (old) — 老 pictures an old person with long hair leaning on a staff; the short form 耂 is also in 考 test and 孝 filial.
人 (person) — a side-view figure of a person walking. As a radical it appears as 亻 on the left: 你 他 们.

example.hanzi: 那位老人每天早上散步。
example.pinyin: nà wèi lǎorén měitiān zǎoshang sànbù.
example.english: That elderly person takes a walk every morning.
example.fact: Jeanne Calment of France holds the verified record for the longest human lifespan, living to 122 years and 164 days before her death in 1997. She was born the same year the Eiffel Tower was built and reportedly still rode a bicycle until she was 100. Gerontologists still study her case closely because no other verified case has come close to matching it.

examples.hanzi: 我想让老人坐在这里。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng ràng lǎorén zuò zài zhèlǐ.
examples.english: I'd like to let the elderly person sit here.

examples.hanzi: 这个小区有很多老人。
examples.pinyin: Zhège xiǎoqū yǒu hěn duō lǎorén.
examples.english: This neighborhood has a lot of elderly people.

components.note: 氵 (water) — water and flow, as in 河, 海, 清: water draining away.
肖 (xiāo) gives the exact sound; also in 销 xiāo and 削 xuē.
阝 (hill, from 阜) — marks slopes and barriers, as in 院, 阶, 障; 防 is a dike to guard against floods, then to defend.
方 (fāng) gives the sound: 防 fáng is close, as in 房 fáng and 妨 fáng.

example.hanzi: 消防队员迅速赶到了现场。
example.pinyin: xiāofáng duìyuán xùnsù gǎndào le xiànchǎng.
example.english: The firefighters quickly arrived at the scene.
example.fact: Ancient Rome established one of the earliest organized firefighting forces, the Vigiles, under Emperor Augustus around 6 AD, after a series of devastating city fires. The force, made up of thousands of men, also served as a night watch and rudimentary police patrol across Rome's crowded districts. Before the Vigiles, Rome had relied on private fire brigades, some of which were accused of extorting owners of burning buildings before agreeing to help.

examples.hanzi: 消防车很快赶到了。
examples.pinyin: Xiāofángchē hěn kuài gǎn dào le.
examples.english: The fire engine arrived very quickly.

examples.hanzi: 这栋楼的消防设备很齐全。
examples.pinyin: Zhè dòng lóu de xiāofáng shèbèi hěn qíquán.
examples.english: The fire safety equipment in this building is complete.

components.note: 方 (square, direction) — early picture is disputed (a plough-like tool or lashed boats). Sound clue in 房 fáng, 防 fáng, 访 fǎng, 放 fàng.
亠 (lid) — the top. Memory aid: a lid over a bent shape — a square-cornered 'side' or place, as in 地方, 方法.
木 (tree) — wood, as in 桌, 树, 板: 案 is a wooden table.
安 (ān) is a close sound clue for àn; also in 按 àn.

example.hanzi: 我们需要一个新的方案。
example.pinyin: wǒmen xūyào yī gè xīn de fāng'àn.
example.english: We need a new plan.
example.fact: The Marshall Plan, launched in 1948, funneled about $13 billion in U.S. aid into rebuilding the economies of Western Europe after the devastation of World War II. Named after Secretary of State George Marshall, the plan is widely credited with helping stabilize European democracies and preventing the spread of communism during the early Cold War. It remains one of the most studied examples of large-scale economic recovery planning in modern history.

examples.hanzi: 你们有什么好方案吗？
examples.pinyin: Nǐmen yǒu shénme hǎo fāng'àn ma?
examples.english: Do you have any good plans?

examples.hanzi: 这个方案太贵了，我们再想想。
examples.pinyin: Zhège fāng'àn tài guì le, wǒmen zài xiǎngxiang.
examples.english: This plan is too expensive; let's think again.

components.note: 彡 (patterns, hairlines) — marks shape, shadow and decoration, as in 影 shadow, 彩 colour; 形 is a shape.
开 (a worn-down 幵) hints at the sound: 形 xíng sounds like 刑 and 型.
宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家, 安, 室: a building holds things.
谷 (valley) — a hollow that holds: 容 is to hold or allow.

example.hanzi: 我不知道怎么形容这种感觉。
example.pinyin: wǒ bù zhīdào zěnme xíngróng zhè zhǒng gǎnjué.
example.english: I don't know how to describe this feeling.
example.fact: Honeybees communicate the direction and distance of food sources to their hive-mates through a precise movement called the waggle dance, discovered by Austrian scientist Karl von Frisch. The angle of the dance relative to the sun shows direction, while the duration of the waggling shows how far away the food is. Von Frisch won the Nobel Prize in 1973 for decoding this remarkably detailed form of animal communication.

examples.hanzi: 你能形容一下他的样子吗？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ néng xíngróng yíxià tā de yàngzi ma?
examples.english: Can you describe what he looks like?

examples.hanzi: 没有话可以形容这里的美。
examples.pinyin: Méiyǒu huà kěyǐ xíngróng zhèlǐ de měi.
examples.english: There are no words to describe the beauty here.

components.note: 言 (speech) — written 讠 on the left of other characters: a warning is spoken.
敬 (jìng, respect) is a close sound clue for jǐng.
乛 (hook stroke) — the top-left bent stroke and dictionary radical; a stroke grouping with no meaning of its own.
一 (one) — the bottom bar. 卫 is simplified from 衛 (guard); Memory aid: a bar blocking a corner, a guard at the door.

example.hanzi: 门口站着两名警卫。
example.pinyin: ménkǒu zhàn zhe liǎng míng jǐngwèi.
example.english: Two guards are standing at the entrance.
example.fact: The Queen's Guard at Buckingham Palace has stood watch in some form since the 1660s, though the familiar red tunics and bearskin hats became standard in the 19th century. Despite their motionless appearance, guardsmen are trained soldiers who rotate every couple of hours and are permitted to react if a visitor gets too close. The bearskin caps are made from real Canadian black bear fur, a practice that has drawn ongoing debate over animal-welfare alternatives.

examples.hanzi: 警卫不让我们进去。
examples.pinyin: Jǐngwèi bú ràng wǒmen jìnqù.
examples.english: The guard won't let us in.

examples.hanzi: 这栋大楼晚上有警卫值班。
examples.pinyin: Zhè dòng dàlóu wǎnshang yǒu jǐngwèi zhíbān.
examples.english: This building has a guard on duty at night.

components.note: 幺 (tiny thread) — the dictionary story is a cord pulled taut in a frame, so 'to lead'; another account sees a bird net. Origin is disputed.
十 (ten) — the lower bar. Reads shuài to lead (率领) and lǜ for rate (效率, 比率). Memory aid: ten threads pulled together as a rate.

example.hanzi: 这家工厂的成功率很高。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiā gōngchǎng de chénggōnglǜ hěn gāo.
example.english: This factory has a high success rate.
example.fact: 率 has two readings: lǜ means 'rate' (效率 efficiency, 汇率 exchange rate, 概率 probability) and shuài means 'to lead' or 'frank' (率领, 坦率). Statistics words almost always end in -率 lǜ.

examples.hanzi: 这个城市的失业率很低。
examples.pinyin: Zhège chéngshì de shīyèlǜ hěn dī.
examples.english: This city's unemployment rate is low.

examples.hanzi: 工作效率很重要。
examples.pinyin: Gōngzuò xiàolǜ hěn zhòngyào.
examples.english: Work efficiency is very important.

components.note: 矢 (arrow) — arrows were measured for length; 矮 is short, as in 矮个子.
委 (wěi) — close sound: 矮 ǎi. 委 also sounds out 萎 wěi and 诿 wěi.

example.hanzi: 他比哥哥矮一点。
example.pinyin: Tā bǐ gēge ǎi yìdiǎn.
example.english: He is a bit shorter than his brother.
example.fact: 矮 is the opposite of 高 for height of people, buildings and furniture; 低 is used for levels such as 低温. Telling someone 你很矮 is quite blunt, so use 不太高 for politeness.

examples.hanzi: 这张桌子太矮了。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhāng zhuōzi tài ǎi le.
examples.english: This table is too low.

examples.hanzi: 她的个子比我矮。
examples.pinyin: Tā de gèzi bǐ wǒ ǎi.
examples.english: She is shorter than me.

components.note: 木 (tree) — marks trees and wood, as in 林, 桥, 板; 树 is a tree.
对 (duì) is a stand-in for an older sound part 尌 (shù), not a sound clue itself.
木 (tree) — two trees side by side make a grove or forest; compare 森 with three.

example.hanzi: 孩子们在树林里捉迷藏。
example.pinyin: háizimen zài shùlín lǐ zhuōmícáng.
example.english: The children are playing hide-and-seek in the woods.
example.fact: In 2019, scientists identified fossilized tree roots in a quarry near Cairo, New York, belonging to a forest around 386 million years old, the oldest known forest on Earth at the time of the discovery. These early trees had shallow, simple root systems very different from modern trees, and their spread is believed to have changed the planet's climate by pulling large amounts of carbon dioxide out of the atmosphere. Forests like this one likely helped set the stage for the diverse ecosystems that followed.

examples.hanzi: 我们在树林里散步。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen zài shùlín lǐ sànbù.
examples.english: We took a walk in the woods.

examples.hanzi: 树林里传来鸟叫声。
examples.pinyin: Shùlín lǐ chuánlái niǎo jiào shēng.
examples.english: Birds can be heard singing in the woods.

components.note: 至 (arrive) — 到 is to arrive.
刂 is the knife form 刀 (dāo), a close sound clue for dào; 到 itself sounds out 倒 dǎo/dào.
此 (cǐ) is a sound clue for 紫 zǐ, 雌 cí and 些 xiē; as a word it means "this".
力 (strength) — visible inside 为. Memory aid: putting strength 力 into doing something; 为 is 'to do, to act' and, in 因为, 为什么, 'because/for'.
為 (traditional) — often explained as a hand leading an elephant to work. 为 is a cursive simplification, so the picture is no longer visible.
止 (stop) — a picture of a foot planted on the ground: where the foot stops. Seen in 步 step (two feet) and 正 correct.

example.hanzi: 今天的讨论就到此为止。
example.pinyin: jīntiān de tǎolùn jiù dàocǐwéizhǐ.
example.english: Today's discussion ends here.
example.fact: The Kármán line, set at 100 kilometers above sea level, is the internationally recognized boundary where Earth's atmosphere effectively ends and outer space begins. It's named after Hungarian-American engineer Theodore von Kármán, who calculated the altitude at which a vehicle would need to travel faster than orbital velocity just to get enough lift from the thin air. Crossing this line is the marker many space agencies use to officially certify someone as an astronaut.

examples.hanzi: 我们的谈话就到此为止吧。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen de tánhuà jiù dàocǐwéizhǐ ba.
examples.english: Let's end our conversation here.

examples.hanzi: 今天的课到此为止，大家下课吧。
examples.pinyin: Jīntiān de kè dàocǐwéizhǐ, dàjiā xiàkè ba.
examples.english: That's all for today's class; you may go.

components.note: 一 (one) — a single horizontal stroke is the number one; 二 and 三 just add strokes, so the first three numbers are tally marks.
無 (traditional) — began as a person dancing with ornaments (same root as 舞). 'None' is a borrowed sense; 无 is an old variant of 無 and the shape does not explain it.
斤 (axe) — cutting tools, as in 新 new and 斩 chop. 所 once echoed the sound of chopping; "place" and "that which" are later borrowed uses.
口 (mouth) — knowing is something you can say aloud; 口 sits in many speech words (问 ask, 告 tell).
矢 (shǐ, arrow) is only a loose sound clue today; the same 知 sound is in 智 zhì (wisdom).

example.hanzi: 他对这件事一无所知。
example.pinyin: tā duì zhè jiàn shì yīwúsuǒzhī.
example.english: He knows nothing about this matter.
example.fact: The Dunning-Kruger effect, identified by psychologists David Dunning and Justin Kruger in 1999, describes how people with very little knowledge of a subject often overestimate how much they actually understand. Their original study had participants rate their own skill in areas like grammar and humor, and the least competent consistently ranked themselves as far more capable than they were. The researchers argued that the same lack of skill that causes poor performance also makes it hard to recognize that the performance is poor.

examples.hanzi: 对中国历史，我几乎一无所知。
examples.pinyin: Duì Zhōngguó lìshǐ, wǒ jīhū yìwúsuǒzhī.
examples.english: I know almost nothing about Chinese history.

examples.hanzi: 他对电脑一无所知。
examples.pinyin: Tā duì diànnǎo yìwúsuǒzhī.
examples.english: He knows nothing at all about computers.

components.note: 禾 (grain) — crops and harvests: 秋 autumn, 种 plant, 秒 second; 利 shows grain 禾 cut with a blade 刂, hence profit and sharp.
皿 (dish) — marks vessels, as in 盘, 盒, 盖; 益 shows water overflowing a dish: more than enough, hence benefit. 溢 yì (overflow) adds water to it.

example.hanzi: 公司应该考虑员工的利益。
example.pinyin: gōngsī yīnggāi kǎolǜ yuángōng de lìyì.
example.english: The company should consider the employees' interests.
example.fact: Clownfish live nestled within the stinging tentacles of sea anemones, protected from predators by a special mucus coating that keeps them from being stung. In return, the clownfish chases off anemone-eating fish and its waste provides the anemone with nutrients. Both species benefit enough from the arrangement that clownfish rarely survive long in the wild without a host anemone nearby.

examples.hanzi: 这样做对大家都有利益。
examples.pinyin: Zhèyàng zuò duì dàjiā dōu yǒu lìyì.
examples.english: Doing this is in everyone's interest.

examples.hanzi: 他们为了各自的利益争吵起来。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen wèile gèzì de lìyì zhēngchǎo qǐlai.
examples.english: They started arguing over their own interests.

components.note: 寸 (inch, hand) — measuring and hands: 对, 导, 寺; 寻 traditionally meant stretching arms to measure, then searching.
求 (seek) — the original picture of a fur coat (裘 qiú adds 衣); "seek, request" is a borrowed use. 求 sounds out 球 qiú and 救 jiù.

example.hanzi: 他正在寻求专业的帮助。
example.pinyin: tā zhèngzài xúnqiú zhuānyè de bāngzhù.
example.english: He is seeking professional help.
example.fact: Pacific salmon can travel thousands of kilometers from the ocean back to the exact freshwater stream where they hatched, guided in part by their acute sense of smell. Scientists believe salmon imprint on the unique chemical signature of their home stream as juveniles and use it years later to find their way back to spawn. Many die shortly after completing this final journey, having spent nearly all their remaining energy reaching it.

examples.hanzi: 我们需要向老师寻求建议。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen xūyào xiàng lǎoshī xúnqiú jiànyì.
examples.english: We need to seek advice from the teacher.

examples.hanzi: 她到处寻求工作机会。
examples.pinyin: Tā dàochù xúnqiú gōngzuò jīhuì.
examples.english: She is looking everywhere for job opportunities.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — marks speech, sounds and eating, as in 叫 call, 吃 eat, 唱 sing; 吼 is roaring or shouting.
孔 (kǒng) — loose sound hint (hǒu vs kǒng).

example.hanzi: 别对我吼，我听得见。
example.pinyin: Bié duì wǒ hǒu, wǒ tīng de jiàn.
example.english: Don't yell at me; I can hear you.
example.fact: 吼 is stronger than 喊: it is an angry or powerful shout, and also the roar of a lion or the howl of wind. 怒吼 means 'to roar in anger', and 狮子吼 is a lion's roar.

examples.hanzi: 老师生气了,大声吼了一句。
examples.pinyin: Lǎoshī shēngqì le, dàshēng hǒu le yí jù.
examples.english: The teacher got angry and shouted a sentence.

examples.hanzi: 狮子在远处吼叫。
examples.pinyin: Shīzi zài yuǎnchù hǒujiào.
examples.english: A lion is roaring in the distance.

components.note: 讠 (speech, simplified 言) — speech and talking: 说, 计, 谈; 设 is to set up or plan by instruction.
殳 (shū, hand holding a tool) is only a loose sound clue; also in 投 tóu and 股 gǔ.

example.hanzi: 公司的总部设在上海。
example.pinyin: Gōngsī de zǒngbù shè zài Shànghǎi.
example.english: The company's headquarters is based in Shanghai.
example.fact: 设 is the root of 设计 (design), 设备 (equipment), 设置 (to set) and 假设 (to suppose). Alone, as in 设在 'is located at', it is a formal verb used for institutions and offices.

examples.hanzi: 他们在公园里设了一个摊位。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen zài gōngyuán li shè le yí ge tānwèi.
examples.english: They set up a stall in the park.

examples.hanzi: 这家酒店的设施很齐全。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā jiǔdiàn de shèshī hěn qíquán.
examples.english: This hotel's facilities are complete.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — words passed down through ten 十 generations of mouths — old; 古 also sounds out 姑 gū and 故 gù.
巴 (bā) — 巴 gives the sound bā in 爸 bà, 吧 ba, 把 bǎ and 疤 bā, so it is a useful sound clue.

example.hanzi: 我们明年打算去古巴旅行。
example.pinyin: wǒmen míngnián dǎsuàn qù gǔbā lǚxíng.
example.english: We plan to travel to Cuba next year.
example.fact: Cuba trains far more doctors relative to its population than most countries in the world, and for decades it has sent thousands of them abroad on medical missions to other nations. This 'medical diplomacy' has become one of Cuba's most significant exports, generating both revenue and international goodwill despite the country's broader economic isolation. Some of these missions have responded to major disease outbreaks, including Ebola in West Africa in 2014.

examples.hanzi: 古巴是一个美丽的岛国。
examples.pinyin: Gǔbā shì yí ge měilì de dǎoguó.
examples.english: Cuba is a beautiful island nation.

examples.hanzi: 我朋友去过古巴，说那里的音乐很有名。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ péngyou qù guo Gǔbā, shuō nàlǐ de yīnyuè hěn yǒumíng.
examples.english: My friend has been to Cuba and says the music there is famous.

components.note: 攵 (tap, strike) — hand with stick, as in 教, 改, 放: to gather by force or hand.
丩 (jiū) is only a loose sound clue for shōu.
回 (return) — a swirl or whirlpool drawn as nested squares: it turns around and comes back.

example.hanzi: 公司决定收回那批产品。
example.pinyin: gōngsī juédìng shōuhuí nà pī chǎnpǐn.
example.english: The company decided to recall that batch of products.
example.fact: In 1982, seven people in the Chicago area died after taking Tylenol capsules that had been laced with cyanide by someone tampering with bottles on store shelves. Johnson & Johnson recalled roughly 31 million bottles nationwide, an enormous and costly response that is still cited as a model for corporate crisis management. The incident led directly to the tamper-resistant packaging now standard on medicine bottles worldwide.

examples.hanzi: 老板收回了之前的决定。
examples.pinyin: Lǎobǎn shōuhuí le zhīqián de juédìng.
examples.english: The boss took back his earlier decision.

examples.hanzi: 他想把借出去的钱收回来。
examples.pinyin: Tā xiǎng bǎ jiè chūqù de qián shōuhuílai.
examples.english: He wants to get back the money he lent out.

components.note: 发 (send out, hair) — two characters merged in simplified writing: 發 fā "emit, issue" and 髮 fà "hair" (头发).
力 (strength) — effort and motion, as in 办, 助, 努. The part 云 stands in for 重 in the traditional 動, which was the sound clue.

example.hanzi: 他一发动汽车就出发了。
example.pinyin: tā yī fādòng qìchē jiù chūfā le.
example.english: As soon as he started the car, he set off.
example.fact: The Soviet Union launched Sputnik 1 on October 4, 1957, the first artificial satellite to orbit Earth, sending the world into the Space Race. The satellite itself was a simple aluminum sphere about the size of a beach ball, but its beeping radio signal, audible to amateur radio operators worldwide, was enough to shock the American public and government. It stayed in orbit for three months before burning up as it reentered the atmosphere.

examples.hanzi: 冬天车子很难发动。
examples.pinyin: Dōngtiān chēzi hěn nán fādòng.
examples.english: Cars are hard to start in winter.

examples.hanzi: 他们发动了一场环保活动。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen fādòng le yì chǎng huánbǎo huódòng.
examples.english: They launched an environmental campaign.

components.note: 忄 (heart) — feelings, as in 快, 忙, 情: a strange feeling.
圣 here is not the "sage" word; it is only a loose sound clue for guài.
异 (simplified 異) — means different or strange; its yì sound also appears in 翼 yì (wing).

example.hanzi: 他最近的行为很怪异。
example.pinyin: tā zuìjìn de xíngwéi hěn guàiyì.
example.english: His recent behavior has been very strange.
example.fact: Axolotls, a type of salamander native to a few lakes in Mexico, can regrow entire limbs, parts of their heart, and even sections of their own brain and spinal cord without scarring. Scientists study this ability closely, hoping to understand mechanisms that might eventually inform human regenerative medicine. In the wild, axolotls are critically endangered, though they are bred by the thousands in labs and as pets.

examples.hanzi: 夜里房子里传来怪异的声音。
examples.pinyin: Yèlǐ fángzi lǐ chuánlái guàiyì de shēngyīn.
examples.english: Strange sounds came from the house at night.

examples.hanzi: 他穿着一件怪异的衣服。
examples.pinyin: Tā chuān zhe yí jiàn guàiyì de yīfu.
examples.english: He's wearing a strange outfit.

components.note: 心 (heart) — a picture of a heart. Written 忄 on the left (快, 怕) and 心 at the bottom (想, 思, 忘); it marks feelings and thoughts.
⻊ (foot, form of 足) — feet and walking: 跑 run, 踢 kick, 路 road, 跟 follow; 跳 is a jump.
兆 (zhào) is a loose hint; the series 桃 táo, 逃 táo, 挑 tiāo, 眺 tiào shares the -ao sound.

example.hanzi: 运动后他的心跳加快了。
example.pinyin: yùndòng hòu tā de xīntiào jiākuài le.
example.english: After exercising, his heartbeat sped up.
example.fact: A blue whale's heart can weigh as much as a small car, and researchers who attached sensors to one recorded a resting heart rate as low as two beats per minute while diving. That same heart can race up to around 37 beats per minute at the surface after a dive, one of the largest heart-rate swings recorded in any animal. Some researchers have suggested that a blue whale's massive heart may be operating close to the physical limit of what a heart of that size can do.

examples.hanzi: 我能听到自己的心跳。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ néng tīng dào zìjǐ de xīntiào.
examples.english: I can hear my own heartbeat.

examples.hanzi: 看到他，我的心跳突然加快了。
examples.pinyin: Kàn dào tā, wǒ de xīntiào tūrán jiākuài le.
examples.english: Seeing him, my heartbeat suddenly sped up.

components.note: 隹 (short-tailed bird) — birds: 难, 雀, 雄; 集 is birds 隹 gathered on a tree 木: to gather.
囗 (enclosure) — boundaries: 国, 园, 围; 团 is a round group. Its traditional form had 專 as sound, like 转 zhuǎn and 传 chuán.

example.hanzi: 这家集团在多个国家有业务。
example.pinyin: zhè jiā jítuán zài duō gè guójiā yǒu yèwù.
example.english: This conglomerate has business in many countries.
example.fact: Berkshire Hathaway, the conglomerate run for decades by Warren Buffett, started out in the 19th century as a textile manufacturing company before Buffett took it over in 1965 and shifted it toward insurance and investment. Today it owns dozens of businesses outright, from Dairy Queen to Duracell, alongside large stock stakes in companies like Apple. Buffett has described the conglomerate structure as letting him move capital freely between businesses without the tax costs of buying and selling them separately.

examples.hanzi: 我哥哥在一家大型集团工作。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ gēge zài yì jiā dàxíng jítuán gōngzuò.
examples.english: My older brother works for a large group company.

examples.hanzi: 这个集团的老板很有名。
examples.pinyin: Zhège jítuán de lǎobǎn hěn yǒumíng.
examples.english: The owner of this group is well known.

components.note: 土 (earth) — ground and place, as in 场 field, 城 city, 坐 sit.
也 (yě) is a loose sound clue for dì; 也 also sounds out 他 tā and 池 chí.
钅 (metal, from 金) — marks metals, as in 钱 money, 银 silver, 钢 steel; 铁 is iron.
失 (shī) is only a loose hint for tiě.

example.hanzi: 我每天坐地铁上班。
example.pinyin: wǒ měitiān zuò dìtiě shàngbān.
example.english: I take the subway to work every day.
example.fact: The London Underground opened in 1863, making it the world's first underground passenger railway, and its early trains ran on steam power through gas-lit tunnels. Because it was decades ahead of comparable systems elsewhere, planners had to invent much of the tunneling and ventilation technology as they went. Today it carries over a billion passenger journeys a year across more than 400 kilometers of track.

examples.hanzi: 这趟地铁几点到？
examples.pinyin: Zhè tàng dìtiě jǐ diǎn dào?
examples.english: What time does this subway arrive?

examples.hanzi: 坐地铁比开车快多了。
examples.pinyin: Zuò dìtiě bǐ kāichē kuài duō le.
examples.english: Taking the subway is much faster than driving.

components.note: 讠 (speech, from 言) — marks talk and questions, as in 说, 问, 请; 询 is to ask.
旬 (xún) gives the sound exactly: 询 xún.
门 (mén, gate) is a close sound clue for wèn; the picture is asking at a gate, as in 闻 wén.
口 (mouth) — speaking, as in 吃, 唱, 叫: asking is a mouth action.

example.hanzi: 他向前台询问了房间的价格。
example.pinyin: tā xiàng qiántái xúnwèn le fángjiān de jiàgé.
example.english: He asked the front desk about the room price.
example.fact: The Socratic method, named after the ancient Greek philosopher Socrates, is a technique of teaching and inquiry built entirely around asking a careful sequence of questions rather than giving direct answers. Socrates reportedly used it in the marketplaces of Athens to expose contradictions in what people claimed to know. The method is still widely used today in law schools, where professors question students to expose the weaknesses in their legal reasoning.

examples.hanzi: 我想询问一下旅行团的价格。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng xúnwèn yíxià lǚxíngtuán de jiàgé.
examples.english: I'd like to ask about the price of the tour group.

examples.hanzi: 警察询问了几位目击者。
examples.pinyin: Jǐngchá xúnwèn le jǐ wèi mùjīzhě.
examples.english: The police questioned several witnesses.

components.note: 辶 (walk) — movement and roads, as in 这 this, 过 pass, 近 near; a 道 is a road, then a way or principle.
首 (shǒu, head) is only a loose sound hint for dào; 首 also means "head/first", fitting a lead-the-way road.
⻊ (foot, form of 足) — feet and travel: 跑, 跳, 跟; 路 is a road.
各 (gè) is a loose sound clue; same part in 洛 luò, 落 luò, 客 kè.

example.hanzi: 这条道路通向山顶。
example.pinyin: zhè tiáo dàolù tōngxiàng shāndǐng.
example.english: This road leads to the mountaintop.
example.fact: At the height of the Roman Empire, engineers had built over 400,000 kilometers of roads connecting territory from Britain to the Middle East, around 80,000 kilometers of which were paved with stone. These roads were built in layered courses over a foundation, a construction method durable enough that some sections are still walkable, and even drivable, nearly two thousand years later. The network was so central to Roman administration that the saying 'all roads lead to Rome' originally described a literal fact of infrastructure.

examples.hanzi: 前面的道路正在修理。
examples.pinyin: Qiánmiàn de dàolù zhèngzài xiūlǐ.
examples.english: The road ahead is under repair.

examples.hanzi: 他选择了一条不同的人生道路。
examples.pinyin: Tā xuǎnzé le yì tiáo bùtóng de rénshēng dàolù.
examples.english: He chose a different path in life.

components.note: 车 (chariot) — war chariots drawn up in a circle (the top part shows the enclosure): an army camp, hence military.
彐 (hand-like part) — 事 is usually explained as a hand holding a tool or tally, 'handling business' — a hedged reading, not certain.
史 (history, scribe) — shares an ancient root with 事: a hand holding a recording tool. Both are about handling official 'matters'.

example.hanzi: 这个国家增加了军事预算。
example.pinyin: zhège guójiā zēngjiā le jūnshì yùsuàn.
example.english: This country increased its military budget.
example.fact: In 218 BC, the Carthaginian general Hannibal led an army that included dozens of war elephants across the Alps to invade Roman Italy from an unexpected direction. The crossing took about two weeks through early snow, and most of the elephants and a large share of his soldiers died from the cold, falls, and ambushes along narrow mountain paths. Despite the losses, Hannibal went on to win several major battles against Rome over the following years.

examples.hanzi: 他们在边境进行军事演习。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen zài biānjìng jìnxíng jūnshì yǎnxí.
examples.english: They are holding military exercises at the border.

examples.hanzi: 他很喜欢看军事杂志。
examples.pinyin: Tā hěn xǐhuan kàn jūnshì zázhì.
examples.english: He really likes reading military magazines.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — giving by hand; also in 给 give, 拿 take.
肙 (yuān) gives a close sound; it also sounds out 娟 juān and 鹃 juān.

example.hanzi: 他向灾区捐了一些钱。
example.pinyin: Tā xiàng zāiqū juān le yìxiē qián.
example.english: He donated some money to the disaster area.
example.fact: 捐 is the usual verb for donations: 捐款 (donate money), 捐血 (give blood) and 捐赠 (to give, more formal). As a noun it can mean 'a levy or tax', as in older 税捐 or 苛捐杂税 ('exorbitant taxes').

examples.hanzi: 学校组织大家为灾区捐款。
examples.pinyin: Xuéxiào zǔzhī dàjiā wèi zāiqū juānkuǎn.
examples.english: The school organized everyone to donate money for the disaster area.

examples.hanzi: 他每年都向希望小学捐书。
examples.pinyin: Tā měi nián dōu xiàng Xīwàng Xiǎoxué juān shū.
examples.english: Every year he donates books to the Hope Primary School.

components.note: 十 (ten, many) — traditional 協 pairs 十 with three 力 (strength) side by side: many forces joined in effort, so cooperation.
力 (strength) — effort, as in 办, 男, 努; 助 is to lend strength.
且 (qiě) is a loose sound clue for zhù; 且 also sounds out 祖 zǔ, 租 zū and 姐 jiě.

example.hanzi: 警方请求民众协助调查。
example.pinyin: jǐngfāng qǐngqiú mínzhòng xiézhù diàochá.
example.english: The police asked the public to assist with the investigation.
example.fact: Modern CPR technique, combining chest compressions with rescue breathing, was developed and standardized in the 1960s after researchers demonstrated that the combination revived far more cardiac arrest patients than either method alone. The training mannequin used to teach it, known as Resusci Anne, was modeled in part on a death mask cast of an unidentified young woman pulled from the Seine River in Paris in the 1880s. Bystander CPR performed in the first few minutes after cardiac arrest can more than double a person's chance of survival.

examples.hanzi: 请你协助我们完成这项工作。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng nǐ xiézhù wǒmen wánchéng zhè xiàng gōngzuò.
examples.english: Please assist us in completing this work.

examples.hanzi: 在同事的协助下，我很快做完了。
examples.pinyin: Zài tóngshì de xiézhù xià, wǒ hěn kuài zuò wán le.
examples.english: With my colleague's help, I finished quickly.

components.note: 及 (reach) — a hand 又 catching up with a person from behind: to reach, then and; seen in 以及, 及时.
日 (sun) — day and time, as in 晴 clear, 早 early, 明 bright; time was read from the sun.
寸 (cùn) stands in for 寺 sì in the traditional 時; sound clue is loose. 寺 also gives 诗 shī and 持 chí.

example.hanzi: 医生及时赶到了现场。
example.pinyin: yīshēng jíshí gǎndào le xiànchǎng.
example.english: The doctor arrived at the scene in time.
example.fact: Atomic clocks are accurate to within about one second every 100 million years, which is precise enough that GPS satellites depend on them for positioning accurate to within a few meters. Because Earth's rotation is gradually slowing and slightly irregular, timekeepers have occasionally had to insert a 'leap second' into official atomic time to keep clocks in sync with the actual length of a day. As of the early 2020s, scientists were debating whether to abolish leap seconds altogether because they complicate computer systems that rely on precise timing.

examples.hanzi: 谢谢你的及时帮助。
examples.pinyin: Xièxie nǐ de jíshí bāngzhù.
examples.english: Thank you for your timely help.

examples.hanzi: 请及时回复我的邮件。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng jíshí huífù wǒ de yóujiàn.
examples.english: Please reply to my email promptly.

components.note: 走 (run, walk) — movement: 起 rise, 越 cross, 赶 hurry, 趣; 超 is to jump over, surpass.
召 (zhào) is a loose sound clue; same part in 招 zhāo, 绍 shào, 照 zhào.
人 (person) — a side-view figure of a person walking. As a radical it appears as 亻 on the left: 你 他 们.

example.hanzi: 他小时候很喜欢看超人的漫画。
example.pinyin: tā xiǎoshíhou hěn xǐhuan kàn chāorén de mànhuà.
example.english: When he was little, he loved reading Superman comics.
example.fact: Superman was created by writer Jerry Siegel and artist Joe Shuster, two teenagers from Cleveland, and first appeared in Action Comics No. 1 in 1938. The character's success is credited with essentially launching the American superhero comic book industry, inspiring countless imitators within just a few years. An original copy of that first issue sold at auction for over $3 million in 2014, making it one of the most valuable comic books in the world.

examples.hanzi: 我儿子想成为超人。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ érzi xiǎng chéngwéi chāorén.
examples.english: My son wants to become Superman.

examples.hanzi: 他拥有超人的记忆力。
examples.pinyin: Tā yōngyǒu chāorén de jìyìlì.
examples.english: He has a superhuman memory.

components.note: 钅 (metal, from 金) — marks metals, as in 钱, 铁, 银; 销 first meant melting metal, then to sell off.
肖 (xiāo) gives the sound exactly: 销 xiāo, also in 消 xiāo and 宵 xiāo.
口 (mouth) — marks speech and mouths, as in 叫, 问, 吃; selling is done with talk, as in 出售.

example.hanzi: 她在一家公司做销售工作。
example.pinyin: tā zài yī jiā gōngsī zuò xiāoshòu gōngzuò.
example.english: She works in sales at a company.
example.fact: The Greek engineer Hero of Alexandria described a coin-operated vending machine around 215 BC that dispensed holy water at Egyptian temples when a coin was dropped in. The mechanism worked using simple lever physics: the weight of the coin pushed down a lever that opened a valve, and the coin then slid off, closing it again. It's considered one of the earliest known examples of an automated retail sale.

examples.hanzi: 他们的销售成绩很好。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen de xiāoshòu chéngjì hěn hǎo.
examples.english: Their sales results are very good.

examples.hanzi: 这家店主要销售手机和电脑。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā diàn zhǔyào xiāoshòu shǒujī hé diànnǎo.
examples.english: This shop mainly sells phones and computers.

components.note: 辶 (movement, road) — 辶 marks going and moving, as in 过, 进, 送; 迷 is losing one's way.
米 (mǐ) — near sound — 迷 is mí, the same syllable with a different tone.
⻊ (foot, form of 足) — feet and travel: 跑, 跳, 跟; 路 is a road.
各 (gè) is a loose sound clue; same part in 洛 luò, 落 luò, 客 kè.

example.hanzi: 我们在山里迷路了。
example.pinyin: wǒmen zài shān lǐ mílù le.
example.english: We got lost in the mountains.
example.fact: Ants navigate using pheromone trails, chemical scent markers laid down by other ants that have already found food, which is why a broken line of ants can seem to wander before relocating the path. If the trail is disrupted, some species also fall back on the position of the sun and even memorized visual landmarks to avoid getting permanently lost. Desert ants in particular have been shown to count their own steps to gauge how far they've walked from the nest.

examples.hanzi: 我在这个城市总是迷路。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zài zhège chéngshì zǒngshì mílù.
examples.english: I always get lost in this city.

examples.hanzi: 别怕，你迷路了可以给我打电话。
examples.pinyin: Bié pà, nǐ mílù le kěyǐ gěi wǒ dǎ diànhuà.
examples.english: Don't worry; if you get lost, you can call me.

components.note: 亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 做: 体 is a person's body.
本 (root) — the root of a person, the body; the traditional form was 體 with 骨 (bone).
月 (flesh) — ⺼ is the body radical (月 in 脸, 脑); the top is an upside-down baby, so 育 is giving birth and then raising, educating.

example.hanzi: 他从小就喜欢体育运动。
example.pinyin: tā cóngxiǎo jiù xǐhuan tǐyù yùndòng.
example.english: He has loved sports since childhood.
example.fact: The modern Olympic Games were revived in Athens in 1896 by French educator Pierre de Coubertin, nearly 1,500 years after the ancient Greek games had ended. Only 14 countries and around 240 athletes, all men, competed in that first modern Games, compared to more than 10,000 athletes from over 200 countries at recent Summer Olympics. Coubertin's original vision emphasized amateur competition and international goodwill over medals or national rivalry.

examples.hanzi: 体育课上，我们练习跑步。
examples.pinyin: Tǐyù kè shàng, wǒmen liànxí pǎobù.
examples.english: In PE class we practice running.

examples.hanzi: 他想当一名体育老师。
examples.pinyin: Tā xiǎng dāng yì míng tǐyù lǎoshī.
examples.english: He wants to become a PE teacher.

components.note: 纟 (silk thread, simplified 糸) — threads and ties, as in 红, 给, 经; 结 is a knot.
吉 (jí) is a close sound clue for jié; 吉 also sounds out 洁 jié.
讠 (speech, simplified 言) — talking and discussion: 说, 议, 谈; 论 is debate and theory.
仑 (lún) gives the sound; same part in 轮 lún and 伦 lún.

example.hanzi: 我们还没有得出最终结论。
example.pinyin: wǒmen hái méiyǒu déchū zuìzhōng jiélùn.
example.english: We haven't reached a final conclusion yet.
example.fact: Charles Darwin spent nearly 20 years gathering evidence before publishing On the Origin of Species in 1859, reaching the conclusion that species change over time through natural selection acting on inherited variation. He was partly pushed to publish when naturalist Alfred Russel Wallace independently arrived at a strikingly similar conclusion, prompting the two to present their ideas jointly before Darwin's book appeared. The book's central conclusion remains the foundation of modern evolutionary biology.

examples.hanzi: 大家得出的结论是一样的。
examples.pinyin: Dàjiā déchū de jiélùn shì yíyàng de.
examples.english: The conclusion everyone reached is the same.

examples.hanzi: 你别急着下结论。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ bié jí zhe xià jiélùn.
examples.english: Don't rush to a conclusion.

components.note: 平 (píng, flat) also lends its sound to 评 píng, 苹 píng and 坪 píng.
行 (xíng) is a loose hint for héng; 衡 means balance, as in 平衡.

example.hanzi: 骑自行车需要保持平衡。
example.pinyin: qí zìxíngchē xūyào bǎochí pínghéng.
example.english: Riding a bicycle requires keeping your balance.
example.fact: The sense of balance relies mainly on the vestibular system in the inner ear, which uses fluid-filled canals to detect the position and motion of the head. In the near-weightlessness of space, this system gets confused because it can no longer rely on gravity as a reference, which is why many astronauts experience disorientation and motion sickness during their first days in orbit. Most astronauts adapt within a few days as their brains learn to rely more on vision to judge orientation.

examples.hanzi: 要平衡工作和生活并不容易。
examples.pinyin: Yào pínghéng gōngzuò hé shēnghuó bìng bù róngyì.
examples.english: Balancing work and life isn't easy.

examples.hanzi: 走在窄窄的木板上，他失去了平衡。
examples.pinyin: Zǒu zài zhǎizhǎi de mùbǎn shàng, tā shīqù le pínghéng.
examples.english: Walking on the narrow plank, he lost his balance.
